messages:
Noah (SRE): Quick follow-up from last night's repeated short latency bursts. We observed ~6m p95 excursions to ~1.5s driven by a small set of heavy callers and cache churn. Need concrete owners and a defined SLO safety path that doesn't break enterprise SLAs.

Priya (Platform): Agreed. My suggestion: introduce a scoped "escrow" for public keys + an automated fallback routing policy. Prefer to avoid loosening SLAs for enterprise tenants.

Diego (Service Owner): For our endpoints we can tolerate degraded precision on non-enterprise keys (reduced-dim embeddings, async fallback) but we must document which features are affected. I'll own the policy doc.

Claire (Product): We need a communication plan for customers and a clear list of enterprise vs public tenants. Also want a dashboard view that shows per-tenant burn-rate and a top-callers export.

Noah (SRE): Concrete proposal: temporary safety plan for 14 days: public-hosted p95 <= 320ms (was 200ms) as a scoped SLO only applied to non-enterprise API keys. p99 remains as-is. Add automatic pause of non-critical rollouts if 72h burn-rate > 1.4. If possible, prefer graceful degradation instead of SLO loosen.

Priya (Platform): Implementation plan: 1) label-based routing -> 2% traffic to quantized fallback for public keys today, expand to 10% if 24h burn-rate > 1.5 2) label-scoped "error-budget escrow" that buffers short spikes for public keys only 3) add Prometheus panels for per-key p95 and burn-rate and CSV export for top callers.

Diego (Service Owner): I'll draft the degradation matrix for /generate, /embed, /chat: which features to reduce and thresholds for switching. ETA 48h.

Claire (Product): I'll prepare the customer comms template and enterprise mapping doc. ETA tomorrow. We'll only apply fallback to listed public keys after Sales ack.

Noah (SRE): Action items and ownerships: - Noah: Add burn-rate alerts + playbook snippet to SLO dashboard; add "top callers by p95" CSV export (today) - Priya: Implement 2% quantized canary + label routing; add escrow config (today) - Diego: Draft degradation policy and enterprise exemption list (48h) - Claire: Customer comms + internal FAQ + notify Sales (tomorrow) - ops-bot: create a remediation checkpoint event and configure alerting group

ops-bot: Created calendar event "SLO remediation checkpoint" Mon 09:15 PT and alert group p95 burn-rate > 1.2 -> notify #eng-sre + oncall.

Priya (Platform): PromQL snippets I'll add to the dashboard: p95 per key: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, api_key, route)) and burn-rate: increase(error_budget_spent_total{tier="public"}[1d]) / increase(error_budget_total{tier="public"}[1d]).

Noah (SRE): We should also add a recurring-pattern detector to the postmortem tracker to auto-tag incidents that match: short high-amplitude spikes + concentrated caller set. That way owners get alerted to recurring patterns instead of re-triaging each time.

Priya (Platform): I can prototype a simple detector that looks for >3 spikes in 7d with topk callers overlap > 0.6 Jaccard. Zoe in data-eng might help if we want a more robust model.

Diego (Service Owner): For enterprise exemption: list includes keys prefixed with "ent-" and any tenant in the Sales "SLA-Enterprise" list. I'll sync with Sales and post the list here.

Claire (Product): I'll post the comms draft to #customer-ops for review before we flip any routing. Also adding a short decision table: when escrow applies vs when we immediately enforce SLA.

Noah (SRE): Temporary routing plan: enable 2% canary to quantized variants for non-enterprise keys immediately. If 24h burn-rate > 1.4 expand to 10% and rate-limit top 5 callers with exponential backoff. If 72h burn-rate > 1.4 pause non-critical automated deploys.

Priya (Platform): Opened PR for routing and escrow config (https://git.internal/platform/PR-1123). Includes dashboard panels and playbook updates. Requesting reviews from Noah and Diego.

Noah (SRE): I've updated the runbook snippet: on short spike -> check escrow status -> prefer degraded path for public keys -> notify owners -> run canary checks -> revert when stable for 2h. Added CSV export for top callers to help product triage.

Diego (Service Owner): I'll prepare the degradation policy and feature list. Will include exact endpoints and a test plan to ensure enterprise keys are unaffected.

Claire (Product): Noted. Follow-up sync scheduled via ops-bot. Please add your action items to the postmortem tracker with owner+due date. We'll review progress in the checkpoint.

Noah (SRE): Closing note: preference is graceful degradation > SLO loosen. The temporary SLO safety window is a last-resort safety valve to keep customer-facing SLAs intact for paying tenants. Update this thread with any changes.
